favourite.heading: Why Virginia can pull away
bullets: Virginia is the better football team by 11.4 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 74% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+11.4 pts).
Playing at Virginia is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).
Conference strength differs and the in-season sample is still thin, worth 3.9 points to Virginia (+3.9 pts).
Stylistically the matchup favours Virginia by 1.3 points: ball control vs front disruption (+1.3 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Delaware can keep it close
bullets: The outcome range is 15.3 points wide at one sigma — p10 -2.3 to p90 +41.7 for Virginia, so a projection of +20.7 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 4%.
College ratings are built on twelve-game seasons against wildly uneven schedules; even a clean rating gap carries more estimation error than the number implies.
